meta.detector: omna_core unified L1-L6 engine, measured THROUGH the Python library (the same path df.omna.mask_pii / pii_report use)
meta.dataset: Gretel PII Benchmark (Gretel AI / NVIDIA) — gretel-pii-masking-en
meta.methodology: Identical to the original 2026-04-28 run: gold spans from the `entities` column; a detection is a TP when it overlaps a gold span by >=1 char in the same text; greedy one-to-one matching. ONLY the detector changed (was Presidio), so these are like-for-like with the prior core-PII figures.

core_pii.description: Gold limited to name / email / phone / SSN / credit-card
core_pii.note: Recall 0.840 with the model is well above the prior Presidio-based path (0.692) — the engine catches more core PII. The low core-PII PRECISION is a scoring artifact: the engine detects 30+ PII types, but this slice's gold contains only 5, so correct detections of the other 25+ types are counted as false positives here. See all_types for the fair precision.

all_types.description: Gold = all PII types present in the dataset

coverage.entity_types: 30+ (people, gov/national IDs, financial, health, employment, digital/network)
coverage.secret_rules: 220+ (AWS keys, GitHub tokens, JWTs, private keys, ...) with entropy checks
coverage.validated_ids: 30+ international schemes with checksum validation (Luhn, IBAN mod-97, Verhoeff, NHS, ...)
coverage.secrets_policy: always irreversibly [REDACTED:KIND]; never written to the reversible token map
